title: Polyglot QuickForge starter runbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, pragmatic runbook to get an engineering team from zero to a reproducible smoke demo that exercises Redwood SDKs in 3 languages (Python, TypeScript, and Go) and validates telemetry + fallback behavior. The goal is a 30–45 minute guided lab for an internal hackbench, customer proof-of-concept, or Solutions pairing session.

Audience:
- Integrators and SDK maintainers who need a repeatable mini-lab to demonstrate common integration flows.
- Solutions engineers running a live customer session.
- Internal hackathon participants who want a low-friction, observable example.

Non-goals:
- This is not a full production integration guide. It focuses on the minimal happy path plus two common failure modes (network latency + model fallback).

High-level flow (approx timings):
- 0–5m: environment prep (install, creds)
- 5–20m: run sample app in each language and confirm predictions
- 20–30m: inject failure scenarios (latency, quota) and observe fallback/telemetry
- 30–45m: add a small customization (prefix cache) and measure token counts/cost

Prereqs (short):
- Local machine with Docker (optional) and a Node/Python/Go toolchain
- Redwood test API key (scoped to demo project) and a sandbox project in Console
- Git clone of the quickforge-examples repo (linked in artifacts)

Quick setup commands (copy/paste):
- git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickforge-examples.git quickforge
- cd quickforge
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk-test-XXX"

Python (5–8m):
- cd python-sample
- python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
- pip install -r requirements.txt
- python run_demo.py --model gpt-small --prompt-file ../prompts/simple.txt
Expected: printed 1 response, logs show latency and token counts to stdout.

TypeScript (5–8m):
- cd ts-sample
- npm ci && npm run build
- REDWOOD_API_KEY=$REDWOOD_API_KEY node dist/run_demo.js --model gpt-small --prompt ../prompts/simple.txt
Expected: streaming output to console, telemetry event emitted to local file telemetry.json

Go (5–8m):
- cd go-sample
- go run ./cmd/demo --model gpt-small --prompt ../prompts/simple.txt
Expected: compact binary prints response; a sidecar tracer prints request/response id mapping.

Observability checks (10m):
- Confirm each run emits a telemetry record with: request_id, model, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, region
- Open Console > Projects > quickforge-sandbox and verify per-route latency and cost estimate (approx)
- Validate that token counts in telemetry match SDK-reported counters (spot-check two runs)

Failure scenarios to demonstrate (10m):
1) Artificial latency: run a small proxy (scripts/proxy-sim.sh) to delay responses by 800ms.
   - Expected: SDK circuit breaker trips; fallback to cheaper model variant (gpt-tiny) configured in client fallback.json
   - What to watch: console fallback events, increased error rate in telemetry, model switch recorded
2) Quota exceeded: swap API key to one with a low quota and replay load script (scripts/loadtest.sh)
   - Expected: rate limit responses, SDK retries with exponential backoff, final throttling error surfaced to app

Mini customization (optional, 10m): prefix caching
- Edit samples to enable prefix cache (samples/common/cache_config.yaml) and re-run the Python demo with a repeating prompt.
- Measure tokens_out reduction and confirm cost delta in Console.

Acceptance checklist (for the demo to be considered successful):
- [ ] Three language demos ran end-to-end without code changes (only creds + model name)
- [ ] Telemetry emitted and visible in local telemetry.json and Console
- [ ] At least one failure scenario reproduced and fallback logic observed
- [ ] Token counts before/after enabling cache recorded

Open questions (for follow-up):
- Should the runbook include a prebuilt Docker image for totally hermetic demoing? Pros: consistency. Cons: heavier onboarding time.
- How should we template the telemetry samples to avoid leaking internal project IDs when sharing externally?
- Do Solutions want a condensed 10m variant for Exec demos (remove failure scenarios)?

Next steps / ownership:
- Maya P: finalize scripts and add Dockerfile (target: next week)
- Carlos R: add telemetry scrubber and example output (JIRA-DEV-1832)
- Samir G: author a 10m variant slide deck for Solutions rehearsals

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Keep prompts deliberately simple. Avoid proprietary examples.
- Add a tiny CanCan test that asserts fallback was used (check response model id).
- Remember to mark demo project as ephemeral and auto-delete after 7 days.

References & links: see linked_artifacts at top.

Raw commands and dev hints (for the session):
- If streaming stalls in TS, set NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=1024 for the node process
- If Python venv fails on Windows, fallback to pipx install for isolated runner
- For macOS M1 devs: use brew-installed go/node, some modules have prebuilt arm64 wheels

Revision history:
- 2025-01-12: initial sketch (Maya)
- 2025-01-20: added Go sample notes (Samir)
- 2025-02-02: telemetry scrubber todo added (Carlos)

End of runbook.
